edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia (archive bub_gb_DY2xvRwPetMC), Latin column, Duodecim Capita de Fide, Cap. IX, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 29)

source_text: Si quis dicit mutabilem aut alterabilem Christum, et non confitetur ipsum immutabilem spiritu, corruptibilem carne; anathema sit. Qua ratione potest aliquis dicere, mutabilem aut variabilem esse Christum? cum ipse Dominus dicat: Ego sum, et non mutor. Et rursum: Neque anima eius relicta est in inferno; neque caro eius vidit corruptionem.
thought_title: Christ is not changeable or alterable
orientation: Gregory condemns calling Christ changeable, and answers from Malachi and from the Psalm that Peter applies to Christ in Acts.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says Christ [is] changeable (mutabilem) or alterable (alterabilem), and does not confess him unchangeable (immutabilem) in spirit (spiritu), corruptible (corruptibilem) in flesh (carne); let him be anathema. By what reason can anyone say Christ to be changeable or variable (variabilem)? when the Lord himself says: I am, and I am not changed (non mutor). And again: Neither was his soul (anima) left (relicta) in the underworld (inferno); nor did his flesh see corruption (corruptionem).

choices.why: Printed reading translated; margin al. incorruptibilem disclosed in notes.

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ is changeable or alterable, and does not confess that he is unchangeable in spirit and corruptible in flesh, let him be anathema.

How can anyone say that Christ is changeable or variable, when the Lord himself says, “I am, and I do not change” (Malachi 3:6)? And again, “His soul was not left in the underworld, nor did his flesh see corruption” (Acts 2:31; Psalm 16:10).
notes: DOUBTFUL READING: the text prints corruptibilem carne (“corruptible in flesh”) with an asterisk; the margin gives al. incorruptibilem (“incorruptible”), and the facing Greek prints phtharton te sarki with margin al. aphtharton.
The printed reading is translated; the variant would make the clause “incorruptible in flesh”, which fits the Acts quotation that follows.
Spiritu here means Christ's divine nature, not the Holy Spirit, so it is lower-case; the title avoids taking a side on the variant.
Malachi 3:6 is quoted loosely (Vulgate Ego enim Dominus, et non mutor).
The second quotation is in the third person of Acts 2:31, which applies Psalm 15:10 (Vulgate and LXX numbering; English Psalm 16:10).
Infernus rendered “the underworld” (the realm of the dead), not “hell”.
Margin sigla Malach. 3, Psal. 15 et Act. 2.
